itemListElement.name: Google Ads Quality Score Explained for Local Businesses

mainEntity.name: What is a good Quality Score for a local business?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single "good" number that applies to every trade and keyword. Quality Score is a 1 to 10 diagnostic at the keyword level, and what matters is whether the weak components point at something you can fix. Focus on whether the ad matches the search and the page delivers, then judge the keyword by the calls and customers it brings.

mainEntity.name: Does a higher Quality Score lower my cost per click?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not on its own. Google says Quality Score is not an input in the ad auction. What enters Ad Rank includes your bid and the quality of your ads and landing page, along with factors such as the competitiveness of the auction. Better ads and pages help you compete, but the number is a diagnostic, not a discount.

mainEntity.name: What are the three parts of Quality Score?

acceptedAnswer.text: Expected click-through rate, ad relevance and landing page experience. Each one reflects whether your ad is likely to earn a click, whether it matches the search, and whether the page delivers what the ad promised.

mainEntity.name: Should I pause keywords with a low Quality Score?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. First look at which component is weak and whether the keyword brings real calls at a cost that works for your business. Fix the ad or page if you can, and pause a keyword only when it stays unprofitable after you have addressed the cause.
